findings.reason: a worker implementing §15 as written will find four of the thirteen ids still red with no instruction to re-anchor `test_follow_observes_other_sessions.py`, so the plan must either deliver the own session's rows on a pane that observes another session or name that file as a re-anchor.
findings.text: §15's done-when requires "the thirteen ids pass alone", but its deliverable explicitly keeps the own session's baseline row withheld ("An own-session baseline row, kind `(None, state)`, stays withheld") and delivers only the *observed* session's rows; four of the thirteen ids live in `tests/test_follow_observes_other_sessions.py` and assert the pane shows the **own** session's `(None, "working")` baseline row with a session that is not in the observed set, so under the stated mechanism those rows are still withheld and the ids stay red. Reproduced at base (`base-observes-own-row-withheld.log`): `test_rows_from_an_observed_session_carry_the_foreign_marker_and_own_rows_do_not` fails with `KeyError: 'my-node'` at `tests/test_follow_observes_other_sessions.py:348` and `test_an_observed_session_named_identically_to_the_owning_session_adds_no_duplicate` fails `assert 0 == 1` at line 390 — both because the own-session `my-node` baseline never reaches the pane. The other two ids (`…row_achieves_the_pane_without_falling_out`, `…the_real_configuration_home_gains_no_file`, and `…that_dispatched_nothing_yields_no_rows_and_no_error`) assert the same own row.
